gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each route to a blood-pressure reading actually costs a US buyer today. The cheapest one that also gives a full fitness watch is a Galaxy Watch8 40mm ($299.99 at samsung.com) plus the separate arm cuff Samsung requires for calibration (Omron Bronze BP5150, $46.99 MSRP), $346.98 in total and Galaxy phone only. The others: Hilo Core costs $239.98 in year one and $389.97 over two years. The Huawei Watch D2 is a $409 import. The D3 is sold only as a $659 China-version import. Apple's BP feature (hypertension notifications) starts at $399 on the Series 12.
standout_why: I compared against fitcoin.co (Nov 4), the Hilo Core vs HLTH vs Hume blog (cited) and ChatGPT's own cards. Fitcoin gives Hilo's $89.99 + $149.99/yr and the D3 at £399 but no US price for Samsung, Apple or Huawei. It says Samsung needs 'your own arm cuff' without pricing that cuff. Hilo's blog prices only Hilo, HLTH and Hume. ChatGPT's prices are out of date against the makers' stores today: Watch8 44mm $379.99 (samsung.com: $329.99), Watch9 44mm $409.99 (samsung.com: $459.99; I did not open the Target listing ChatGPT showed), and Apple Watch Series 11 $349 (Apple now sells the Series 12 from $399). ChatGPT also presented the Omron HeartGuide as buyable, but it does not appear in Omron US's current product list. None of these pages adds up the total cost (watch + cuff, or band + subscription over time).
decides: This confirms that for a US shopper who wants fitness tracking plus a BP number, a last-generation Galaxy Watch8 with a $47 validated arm cuff is the cheapest full-watch option (needs a Galaxy phone, wellness use only). The Watch9 adds $130 for no BP difference, since Samsung lists Watch4 and later. A real cuff on the wrist (Huawei D2) costs about $62 more as an unofficial import with no US approval. Hilo is cheaper in year one but costs more by year two, and its band does no fitness tracking. iPhone users get no BP numbers at any price. The Omron HeartGuide should not be recommended because Omron US no longer lists it.
